situation: An Organization's colour and logo reach the Portal a Guest opens
given: an Owner of an Organization, and a Resident with a current Stay at one of its Properties
when: the Owner sets a colour and uploads a logo, and the Resident opens the Portal
then: the Portal's primary buttons and links and its active navigation item carry the colour and its header shows the logo, on the next load; success, warning and destructive colours are the system's
test_name: branding.test.ts: BR-S1-01: a saved colour and logo are what the Resident's Stay reads back; branding.spec.ts: BR-S1-01: the Owner brands the Organization and the Resident's Portal carries the colour and the logo

situation: The colour is one hex value
given: a Staff Member who may manage the brand
when: a colour that is not six hex digits after a # is saved: red, #fff, #12345g, rgb(1,2,3)
then: refused as invalid before any statement runs, and by a check constraint on the table if one got past the module; stored lower-case
test_name: branding-module.test.ts: BR-S1-02: only #rrggbb is a colour; branding.test.ts: BR-S1-02: a value that is not a colour is refused and nothing is written; branding.test.sql: BR-S1-02: a colour that is not #rrggbb is refused by the table

situation: The foreground is derived and never stored
given: a valid brand colour
when: it is read for the Portal
then: the foreground is white or black, whichever has the greater WCAG contrast against the colour; only the colour is stored, so there is no pair that could disagree
test_name: branding-module.test.ts: BR-S1-03: the foreground is whichever of white and black reads better

situation: Any valid colour is accepted, and text on white uses a darker shade of it where the colour itself would not read
given: a brand colour such as the orange #e67e22 or the yellow #ffeb3b, a good fill and a poor link on the white canvas
when: it is saved and the Portal is drawn
then: buttons and filled surfaces use the colour as it is, with a white or black foreground picked by contrast, which always reaches 4.5:1; links, text and focus rings use a darker shade of the same hue as a second token, --primary-text, found by lowering OKLCH lightness until it reaches 4.5:1 against white (the colour itself when it already does); the screen shows both swatches and says the darker one is used for text. This replaces the refusal first specified (a colour where neither white nor black reaches 4.5:1), which could never fire, and then a refusal of any colour under 4.5:1 against white, which rejected most real hotel brands
test_name: branding-module.test.ts: BR-S1-04: any valid colour is accepted and every colour has a text shade of at least 4.5:1 against white; branding-module.test.ts: BR-S1-04: the text shade keeps the hue of the colour; branding-module.test.ts: BR-S1-04: an orange is a fine fill and its text shade is a darker orange; branding.test.ts: BR-S1-04: a light colour is accepted as it is and read back with a darker text shade; branding.spec.ts: BR-S1-04: a light colour is accepted and the screen shows the darker shade used for text; branding.spec.ts: BR-S1-04: a link in the Portal of an orange brand reads at 4.5:1 on white

situation: A logo is accepted by what its bytes say
given: a PNG, a JPEG or a WebP of at most 512 KB, at least 128 px tall and at most 4096 px either way
then: stored with the type, size, width, height and SHA-256 read from the bytes themselves
test_name: branding-module.test.ts: BR-S1-05: a PNG a JPEG and a WebP are read for their type and size from their bytes; branding.test.ts: BR-S1-05: an uploaded logo is stored with the facts read from its bytes

situation: SVG is refused
given: an SVG, with or without script, called logo.png or sent as image/png
then: refused as svg: blueprint 8 allows no executable code, and the table refuses a type outside PNG, JPEG and WebP
test_name: branding-module.test.ts: BR-S1-06: an SVG is refused by name whatever it is called; branding.test.ts: BR-S1-06: an SVG logo is refused and nothing is stored; branding.test.sql: BR-S1-06: a logo typed image/svg+xml is refused by the table

situation: A logo over 512 KB is refused
given: a file of 512 KB and one byte
then: refused as too large before it is parsed, and by a check constraint if it got past the module; exactly 512 KB is accepted
test_name: branding-module.test.ts: BR-S1-07: a logo over 512 KB is refused and one of exactly 512 KB is not; branding.test.sql: BR-S1-07: a logo over 512 KB is refused by the table

situation: A logo must be tall enough and not enormous
given: a PNG 127 px tall, and one 5000 px wide
then: refused as too small or as too large in its dimensions, and by a check constraint on the table; 128 px tall is accepted
test_name: branding-module.test.ts: BR-S1-08: a logo under 128 px tall or over 4096 px is refused; branding.test.sql: BR-S1-08: a logo under 128 px tall is refused by the table

situation: The bytes decide the type and not the name or the claimed type
given: a text file called logo.png, or a JPEG sent as image/png
then: a text file is refused as not an image; the table refuses a content type its bytes do not start with
test_name: branding-module.test.ts: BR-S1-09: a text file named logo.png is not a logo; branding.test.ts: BR-S1-09: a file that is not an image is refused whatever it is called; branding.test.sql: BR-S1-09: a type that is not what the bytes say is refused by the table

situation: The hash and the size are the bytes' own
given: a caller that records a hash or a size other than the bytes'
then: refused by a check constraint: the hash versions the URL and names the logo in the audit record, so it is the database's to vouch for
test_name: branding.test.sql: BR-S1-10: a hash or a size that is not the bytes' own is refused

situation: A damaged, cut or padded image is refused
given: a PNG with no IEND, a wrong IHDR checksum or bytes after its end; a WebP whose RIFF length is not the file's; a JPEG with no end marker, no start marker or bytes after its end; or a file cut short
then: refused as corrupt, with a message that says the file may be damaged; the module reads each PNG chunk's length and checksum, the WebP's declared length against its size, and the JPEG's markers at both ends, before it reads a size
test_name: branding-module.test.ts: BR-S1-11: a truncated image is corrupt; branding-module.test.ts: BR-S1-11: a PNG whose header checksum is wrong, or that has no IEND, or a tail after it, is corrupt; branding-module.test.ts: BR-S1-11: a WebP whose RIFF length is not the file's, and a JPEG with a tail after its end, are corrupt

situation: Reset to default empties the brand and keeps the rows
given: a branded Organization, and an Owner
then: the colour and the logo are empty, the Portal is back to Ranza's theme on the next load, and no row is deleted: ranza_app holds no DELETE on either table
test_name: branding.test.ts: BR-S1-12: a reset empties the brand and keeps the rows; branding.test.sql: BR-S1-12: the application role cannot delete a brand; branding.spec.ts: BR-S1-12: reset returns the Portal to the default theme

situation: The permission is a gate of its own
given: a member who passes every other gate: whole-Organization reach, the Subscription, the Configuration capability
when: they write the brand without branding.manage
then: refused by the insert and update policies of both tables
test_name: branding.test.sql: BR-S1-13: a member without branding.manage writes nothing; branding.test.ts: BR-S1-13: a Manager is refused through the module

situation: Reach is a gate of its own
given: a role holding branding.manage, assigned to one Property
then: refused: the brand has no Property to narrow to, so it takes reach to the whole Organization
test_name: branding.test.sql: BR-S1-14: a holder of the permission who reaches one Property writes nothing

situation: The commercial gates are gates of their own
given: an Owner whose Organization has a suspended Subscription, or no Configuration capability at any Property, or no platform_core Entitlement
then: refused by each; a past_due Subscription is still admitted (ADR 0040)
test_name: branding.test.sql: BR-S1-15: a suspended Subscription writes nothing and a past_due one does; branding.test.sql: BR-S1-15: no Configuration capability and no Entitlement each write nothing

situation: A write names its author
given: an Owner
when: they write a row whose updated_by is somebody else
then: refused by the insert and update policies
test_name: branding.test.sql: BR-S1-16: a write names the acting user as its author

situation: Another Organization's brand is neither read nor written
given: an Owner of Organization A and a brand in Organization B
when: they read or write B's brand or logo
then: nothing is returned and nothing is written
test_name: branding.test.sql: BR-S1-17: an Owner reads and writes nothing of another Organization's brand; branding.test.ts: BR-S1-17: another Organization's brand is not read through the module

situation: A write names its columns
given: the application role, acting for somebody who holds branding.manage across two Organizations
when: it writes a column the commands do not (created_at, a different organization_id, which would move a brand to the other Organization) or deletes a row
then: refused: the grants are column lists and neither table grants DELETE
test_name: branding.test.sql: BR-S1-18: the application role writes only the columns the commands write

situation: The permission is in the catalogue and only the Owner ships with it
given: the permission catalogue and the shipped roles
then: branding.manage is in the catalogue under platform_core and the shipped Owner holds it; Manager, Front desk, Housekeeping and Finance do not
test_name: branding.test.sql: BR-S1-19: branding.manage is in the catalogue and only the shipped Owner holds it

situation: A Resident reads the brand of an Organization they have a current Stay with
given: a Resident with a reserved or in-house Stay at Organization A and none at B
then: A's brand and logo and nothing of B's; a departed or cancelled Stay reads nothing
test_name: branding.test.sql: BR-S1-20: a Resident reads the brand and the logo of the Organization they have a current Stay with and no other; branding.test.ts: BR-S1-20: a Resident of one Organization reads nothing of another's brand

situation: Two Organizations
given: a Resident with a current Stay at Organization A and another at Organization B, each with its own brand
then: each Stay is drawn in its own Organization's colour; the header and its logo follow the Stay the page leads with, the latest to start; the Resident is never told which Organization a brand is
test_name: branding.test.sql: BR-S1-21: a Resident of two Organizations reads both brands; branding.test.ts: BR-S1-21: each Stay of a Resident of two Organizations carries its own brand

situation: A Staff Member who may not manage the brand reads none
given: a Front desk member of the Organization, with no Stay
when: they read the brand through the module or the table
then: nothing: the default brand and canManage false
test_name: branding.test.sql: BR-S1-22: a member without the permission reads no brand and no logo; branding.test.ts: BR-S1-22: a member without the permission is shown the default and told they may not change it

situation: The Portal's sign-in page stays Ranza's
given: a visitor who is not signed in, and an Organization with a brand
when: they open the Portal's sign-in page
then: Ranza's theme: the Organization is not known before the visitor is
test_name: branding.spec.ts: BR-S1-23: the Portal's sign-in page stays Ranza's

situation: The Workspace stays Ranza's
given: an Owner of a branded Organization
when: they work in the Operator Workspace
then: Ranza's theme everywhere in it, the Branding screen included
test_name: branding.spec.ts: BR-S1-24: the Workspace stays Ranza's while the Organization is branded

situation: A change is audited with the old and the new
given: an Owner who changes the colour, the logo, or both
then: one branding.changed record with the colour before and after and the logo as a content hash and a size before and after; the bytes are never recorded and a part that did not change is not named
test_name: branding.test.ts: BR-S1-25: a change is audited with the colour and the logo's hash and size but never its bytes

situation: A reset is audited
given: a branded Organization, and an Owner
then: one branding.reset record with what was there; resetting an Organization that is already the default records nothing
test_name: branding.test.ts: BR-S1-26: a reset is audited and a reset of the default is not

situation: A save that changes nothing records nothing
given: an Owner who saves the colour and the logo that are already set
then: no audit record, and the brand is as it was
test_name: branding.test.ts: BR-S1-27: a save that changes nothing records nothing

situation: A change shows on the next page load and an unchanged logo is cached
given: a logo that has changed since a Resident last loaded the Portal
then: the page links the logo by its new hash so the browser asks again; a request naming the current hash is cacheable for good, any other revalidates by ETag, and a matching ETag is a 304 with no body
test_name: branding-module.test.ts: BR-S1-28: a request naming the current hash is cached for good and any other revalidates; branding-module.test.ts: BR-S1-28: a matching ETag is a 304 with no body

situation: A Staff Member without the permission does not see the screen
given: a Front desk member
when: they look for Branding in the rail or open its URL
then: no rail entry, and the URL shows the page every unreachable screen shows
test_name: branding.spec.ts: BR-S1-29: a Staff Member without branding.manage does not see the Branding screen

situation: Holding the permission at one Property is not holding it across the Organization
given: a role holding branding.manage, assigned to one Property
then: told that the brand is the whole Organization's and what it takes, instead of a form whose every save would be refused
test_name: branding.test.ts: BR-S1-30: a holder who reaches one Property is told they may not change the brand

situation: Two saves at once
given: two Owners saving at the same moment
then: one waits for the other's row lock; each audit record's old value is what that save replaced, so the two records chain
test_name: branding.test.ts: BR-S1-31: two concurrent saves are serialised and their audit records chain

situation: An unexpected failure is reported and not shown
given: the database is unreachable or a defect is hit
then: the screen says something went wrong and to try again, never the exception's text; the exception is logged with the command and the Property
test_name: branding-actions.test.ts: BR-S1-32: an unexpected failure is reported and the screen is told only that it failed

situation: The Branding screen reads right to left in Arabic
given: an Owner reading Arabic
then: the layout mirrors by logical utilities and the colour field stays left to right
test_name: branding.spec.ts: BR-S1-33: the Branding screen reads right to left in Arabic with the colour field left to right

situation: An Organization that never branded is the default theme
given: an Organization with no brand row
then: no colour is set on the page and no logo is shown
test_name: branding.test.ts: BR-S1-34: an Organization that never branded reads as the default

situation: A logo is served only to a Stay's own Resident
given: a Stay that is another person's, a departed one, or one whose Organization has no logo
when: a Resident asks for its logo
then: the same bodiless 404 for each, so the route is no way to learn which Stays or logos exist
test_name: branding.test.ts: BR-S1-35: the logo of a Stay that is not the viewer's own current Stay is not found

situation: A Resident is shown a brand only where the Portal is shown a Stay
given: a Resident with a current Stay at an Organization whose Subscription is suspended, whose Front Office Entitlement is revoked, or at a Property with the Portal switched off
when: the Portal reads the brand and the logo
then: no brand and no logo, as the Stay list shows no Stay; a past_due Subscription is a grace period and still reads (ADR 0040); the logo route answers 404. The policies and the Stay-keyed reads each ask app.resident_can_use_capability(), as the Stay list does
test_name: branding.test.sql: BR-S1-36: a Resident of an Organization whose Subscription is suspended reads no brand and no logo; branding.test.sql: BR-S1-36: a Resident whose Stay is at a Property with the Portal switched off reads no brand; branding.test.sql: BR-S1-36: a past_due Subscription is in its grace period and its Resident still reads the brand (ADR 0040); branding.test.ts: BR-S1-36: a Resident is shown a brand only where the Portal is shown a Stay

situation: A brand that cannot be read does not take the Portal down
given: a Resident with a current Stay, and a database that fails when the brand is read
then: the failure is reported, with the viewer and the error, and the Portal is drawn in the default theme; the Stay page still shows the Stay
test_name: portal-brand-fallback.test.tsx: BR-S1-37: draws the default theme and reports the failure, in the layout; portal-brand-fallback.test.tsx: BR-S1-37: still shows the Stay on the Stay page

situation: The Branding rail entry and page use the gates the policies use
given: an Owner whose Subscription is suspended, whose Entitlement is revoked, or whose Properties have Configuration off; and a holder of the permission who reaches one Property
when: they look for Branding or open it
then: the entry and the page are offered only where the permission and the Configuration capability both hold at a Property (the same gates 1 to 3 the write policies ask); where a gate has failed the page says what every unreachable screen says, and only a holder who lacks reach is told it is reach
test_name: branding.test.ts: BR-S1-38: the Branding screen is offered where the policies would let a save through; branding-page.test.tsx: BR-S1-38: asks for the permission and the Configuration capability together; branding-page.test.tsx: BR-S1-38: says what every unreachable screen says where a gate has failed, not that reach is missing; branding-page.test.tsx: BR-S1-38: says the same where the gate fails between the list and the read; branding-page.test.tsx: BR-S1-38: shows the form to somebody who may change the brand

situation: A Resident reads only the columns the Portal draws
given: the application role, which a Resident reads through as Staff do
then: only organization_id and primary_color of a brand, and the bytes and what is known of a logo; not who wrote it (updated_by) or when (created_at, updated_at)
test_name: branding.test.sql: BR-S1-39: the application role reads the colour of a brand and which Organization it is, and nothing else; branding.test.sql: BR-S1-39: and of a logo its bytes and what is known of them, not who wrote it or when

situation: The logo routes answer only the person the policies let read it, with the headers a logo needs
given: no session, another person's Stay, a departed Stay, an Organization whose Subscription is suspended, and a Resident or an Owner who may
when: each asks for a logo over HTTP
then: 401 without a session; the same bodiless 404 for the Stay that is another's, the departed one and the gated Organization; and on 200 Cache-Control private, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, the stored Content-Type and a Content-Security-Policy that loads nothing. A UUID of any version is accepted
test_name: brand-logo-routes.test.ts: BR-S1-40: the Portal's route looks up a Stay named by a UUID of any version; brand-logo-routes.test.ts: BR-S1-40: the Workspace's route looks up an Organization named by a UUID of any version; brand-logo-routes.test.ts: BR-S1-40: and neither looks up anything that is not one; branding.spec.ts: BR-S1-40: the Portal's logo route answers 401 without a session and 404 for another person's Stay, a departed Stay and a gated Organization; branding.spec.ts: BR-S1-40: the Portal's logo is served private, nosniff, with its stored type and a closed policy; branding.spec.ts: BR-S1-40: the Workspace's logo route answers 401 without a session and 404 to those who may not manage the brand

situation: The Staff read policies each refuse on a gate of their own
given: a holder of branding.manage who reaches one Property, and one who reaches everything where the Configuration capability is off, neither staying anywhere
when: they read the brand or the logo
then: nothing in either case: whole-Organization reach and the commercial gates are each in the read policy and not only in the write policies
test_name: branding.test.sql: BR-S1-41: a holder of the permission who reaches one Property reads no brand, which reach alone refuses; branding.test.sql: BR-S1-41: a holder who reaches everything reads no brand where the Configuration capability is off, which the gate alone refuses

situation: A logo larger than the framework's default request body still gets the logo message
given: an Owner who chooses a logo of 600 KB, or 2 MB
then: the file reaches the module, which refuses it as too large and the screen says so in their language; the server-action body limit is 4 MB so the framework does not refuse it first with an error nobody can read
test_name: branding-module.test.ts: BR-S1-42: a logo of 600 KB or 2 MB is refused as too large, before it is read; branding-actions.test.ts: BR-S1-42: a logo of 600 KB or 2 MB reaches the module whole, and its refusal reaches the screen; branding.spec.ts: BR-S1-42: a logo of 600 KB and one of 2 MB are each told they are too large

situation: A logo is judged the moment it is chosen
given: an Owner who chooses a PNG 300 x 64 px, or a file over 512 KB, or a file that is not an image
when: the file is chosen, before Save
then: the screen says what is wrong with the numbers that broke the rule ("This image is 64 px tall; a logo must be at least 128 px tall."), shows the file name, size and pixels, and Save stays off with a line saying why; a usable file says so. The limits quoted are the branding module's own, which still judges the bytes on save (BR-S1-07, BR-S1-08)
test_name: branding-view.test.tsx: CONFIGURATION-01: a logo shorter than the minimum is refused on the spot, with its size and the limit, and cannot be saved; branding-view.test.tsx: CONFIGURATION-01: a file that is not an image is refused without being decoded; branding-view.test.tsx: CONFIGURATION-01: a second choice replaces the first, even when the first is read last; configuration-audit.spec.ts: CONFIGURATION-01: a logo below the minimum height is refused on the spot, with its size and the limit (en); branding.spec.ts: BR-S1-42: a logo of 600 KB and one of 2 MB are each told they are too large the moment they are chosen

situation: Leaving Branding with a draft asks first
given: an Owner with a colour typed or a logo chosen and not saved
when: they follow a link, the Back arrow included

test_name: branding-view.test.tsx: CONFIGURATION-02: a link is asked about while a colour or a logo is unsaved, and stopped on no; branding-view.test.tsx: CONFIGURATION-02: a link is not asked about when nothing is unsaved; configuration-audit.spec.ts: CONFIGURATION-02: following Back with an unsaved colour asks first, and keeps the draft on no

situation: Reset says what goes before it happens
given: an Owner of an Organization with a saved colour or logo
then: a dialog names the consequence (Guests see Ranza's mark and green theme from their next visit), lists the saved logo and the saved colour that are removed and any unsaved draft, and nothing is written until Reset the brand; Keep the brand writes nothing; Reset is off when the brand is already the default
test_name: branding-view.test.tsx: CONFIGURATION-04: names what goes, runs nothing until confirmed, and keeps the brand on Keep; branding-view.test.tsx: CONFIGURATION-04: there is nothing to reset on a brand that is already the default; configuration-audit.spec.ts: CONFIGURATION-04: Reset names what goes, changes nothing until it is confirmed, and is off when there is nothing to reset; branding.spec.ts: BR-S1-12: reset returns the Portal to the default theme

situation: The colour check is in plain words, with the numbers a click away
given: an Owner who types a colour, or has none
then: no colour is a dashed well in the theme's own green, not a black swatch; a usable colour says which text colour fills use and whether links use a darker shade, in words; the contrast ratios sit under a Contrast details disclosure
test_name: branding-view.test.tsx: draws the well dashed, in the theme's own green, not as a solid swatch; configuration-audit.spec.ts: CONFIGURATION-05, -06, -03: no colour is a dashed theme-green well, the verdict is in plain words with the numbers a click away, and the preview is a Portal; branding.spec.ts: BR-S1-04: a light colour is accepted and the screen shows the darker shade used for text

situation: The preview is the Portal and sits beside the colour
given: an Owner on a phone or a desktop, with or without a logo
then: the preview directly under the colour card draws a small Portal (side menu with Ranza's mark and an active My stay item, a top bar with the logo only when one is chosen or saved, a Primary button and a link) in the typed colour, and on a 375 px screen it is in view while the colour is typed
test_name: configuration-audit.spec.ts: CONFIGURATION-07: on a phone the preview is in view while the colour is typed; configuration-audit.spec.ts: CONFIGURATION-05, -06, -03: no colour is a dashed theme-green well, the verdict is in plain words with the numbers a click away, and the preview is a Portal

given: an Owner with a logo file in a folder
when: they drag it onto the preview or the Logo card
then: proposed, not built: the file is judged exactly as a chosen one is (BR-S1-43) and replaces the draft; comparable systems that take a dropped logo are Mews and Cloudbeds property settings

given: an Organization that wants the Portal on its own domain
then: deferred: blueprint 8 lists it; it needs DNS, certificates and a host-to-Organization lookup before sign-in

given: an Organization that wants its own typefaces
then: deferred: blueprint 8 lists it; the theme ships Geist and IBM Plex Sans Arabic and Arabic needs a face that draws it

given: an Organization whose guests receive email
when: it asks for its own sender and templates
then: deferred: blueprint 8 lists it; needs the notifications module and sender verification

then: deferred: blueprint 8 lists approved mappings; needs the approved list and the copy catalogue to take it

given: an Organization whose Properties present differently
then: deferred: the brand is the Organization's; a per-Property override adds a precedence rule and a second screen

given: an Organization with a logo near the limit, at scale
then: deferred: Postgres is enough for a 512 KB file read once per page load behind a cache header; object storage waits for a second kind of file

situation: A brand name
given: an Organization whose name differs from the Property's
then: deferred: blueprint 8 lists it; the logo's alt text is the Property's name until it exists
